Plan and tend an imaginary garden

Inspired by Community Produce Garden (@lisachandler, historical inventory page 15) and Gardening (@josefan12, page 16). These are fictional practice beds based on the park prototype. Nothing here waters the garden or earns points.

Move the crops

On paper or aloud, start with three beds, from left to right: Carrots, Tomatoes, Leafy greens. In one rotation, each crop moves one bed to the right. The last crop wraps around to the first bed.

How many rotations put Tomatoes in the first bed? Then, without rotating again, swap two neighboring beds to move Carrots into the middle.

Check the layout

After two rotations the order is Tomatoes, Leafy greens, Carrots. Swap the second and third beds to get Tomatoes, Carrots, Leafy greens.

Match each action to a clue

Choose one action for each imaginary bed: water the practice bed, check the support, or look without changing the bed. Name the clue that helped you choose.

  1. The practice carrot bed is marked dry.

    Check the carrot bed

    Water the practice bed. The marker says the bed is dry.

  2. The practice tomato support is loose.

    Check the tomato bed

    Check the support. The loose frame is the clue.

  3. The leafy bed is marked tended, with nothing to fix.

    Check the leafy bed

    Look without changing the bed. You can observe a bed that needs no action.

In the park, open Community Produce Garden → Plan a practice plot from the board or a garden seat for the button version.
